SQLite's default journaling mode - called DELETE journal - works by writing the original page contents to a rollback journal before modifying the database. This approach is simple and reliable, but it causes readers to block writers and vice versa, creating contention in multi-user scenarios. Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) flips this model: changes are appended to a separate WAL file instead of modifying the database file directly. Readers read the original database file while writers append to the WAL file, so readers and writers do not block each other. This makes WAL mode significantly faster for most real-world workloads.
